description: Figure 6(a) is a bar chart illustrating the distribution of datasets over time for the five most frequent researcher locations and all other locations combined, with the x-axis representing the year from 2012 to 2022 and the y-axis representing the number of datasets on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10². The chart uses grouped bars for each year, with each group containing six bars corresponding to the categories: “Other” (blue), “UK” (red), “USA” (orange), “IT” (purple), “IN” (green), and “DE” (brown), as indicated in the legend. The height of each bar reflects the approximate number of datasets for that location in that year, with the “USA” bar consistently being the tallest across most years, indicating the most consistent and highest volume of dataset publication. The “Other” category shows a notable increase in dataset production starting around 2016, while the “UK” and “DE” bars remain relatively low and stable. The bars are not sorted, and no visual emphasis such as shading or outlining is applied to any specific bar.
